title: Python async (asyncio), Part 4: six traps that break async services
tldr: Six mistakes that are legal Python, raise no error where they are written, and pass tests, each measured on Part 3's gateway: a forgotten await that empties the metrics; seller-e's sync SDK called on the loop, which makes the slowest seller 'win' at 900 ms while the four fast ones time out; CPU work, where threads take turns and only a process pool helps; background Tasks that vanish or fail with nobody told; gather, which drops every failure after the first and hides cancellations among its results; a broad except that swallows CancelledError so requests take 1,200 ms against a 250 ms budget; and timeouts that are relabelled as failures or never counted. Each comes with its root cause in the loop's machinery, its signal, its fix and a test. Debug mode and Ruff/mypy as detectors (and why pytest -W error::RuntimeWarning is not enough), then gateway v5 with every fix, sized for 10 times the load, and an interview drill.
